items: Title: Location Exploration Mechanics
Player Safe: Players can navigate, search, read customs, inspect hazards Underroot when it is present in the fiction.
Gm Only: Use the roll only when the player's method, stakes, and consequence are concrete.

No Roll Reveals: Surface read: A concealed web of tunnels and homes carved among roots where off-ledger communities survive below the dangerous surface. Give obvious visible facts freely; roll for meaning, risk, leverage, cost, or a hidden angle.

Rolls: entity-underroot-engage-underroot entity-underroot Engage Underroot Engage Underroot Instinct Knowledge Finesse Presence Instinct Knowledge, Finesse, Presence 13 Choose the trait from the player's method, not the entity type. A flat read of Underroot hides the cost, motive, or useful next step. Critical Success: best possible version of the action; gain Hope and clear 1 Stress. Add an extra benefit that follows from the fiction. Success with Hope: the PC gets what they wanted and gains Hope. Keep the position clean or generous. Success with Fear: the PC gets what they wanted, but the GM gains Fear and introduces a cost, complication, or pressure. Failure with Hope: the PC does not get the full result, but gains Hope and receives a useful thread, clue, or safer next option. Failure with Fear: the PC fails and the GM gains Fear. Fear Spends: Reveal who benefits from the current situation. Make the cost personal without closing off player agency.
Condition Options: No official condition unless a hazard creates Hidden, Restrained, or Vulnerable

Underroot is not a dungeon; it is a concealed neighborhood of root rooms, low lanterns, and people who survive below the route economy. Underroot is the forest's underside: damp passages, glowing fungus, root doors, old animal routes, and the sense that the ground has a memory. The place breaks into usable table spaces: Root tunnel: Twisting roots make walls, ceiling, and handholds. Glowfungus chamber: Soft light turns water drops and old stones into landmarks. Flood pocket: A low chamber holds dark water and hidden movement. Plants and materials: glowfungus shelves, pale root hairs, water moss, small blind flowers. Animals and...

Block1: Underroot Keep hidden communities human, practical, and self-protecting. A concealed web of tunnels and homes carved among roots where off-ledger communities survive below the dangerous surface. Underroot shows who lives under the official map. Underroot is who the route economy left behind, and they survive by knowing things the surface never bothered to learn. Underroot shows who lives under the official map. Trust is the only currency that works down here. Outsiders are watched until they prove they are not a threat to a place that cannot afford one. pages/entities/underroot.html

Block2: Root arches and carved shelves form rooms where the forest is ceiling, wall, and witness. Lanterns are shielded so light does not betray doors above. Air holes are hidden inside harmless knots. The best paths avoid places where footsteps would sound hollow. Detail Cool earth, root sap, cooking smoke kept low, and stored herbs. Detail Walls are ribbed with living root; touching them feels like touching something asleep. Local residents or workers appropriate to the place Centi-Beetles carve low tunnels Spidermanders press ash-damp feet into soft walls Hellbender legends make every tremor feel observed Fox-Bats sleep in warm cracks No default combatant; add only if the scene introduces one Local civic, trade, or route interests Food, tools, route signs, local goods, or scene-specific clues glowfungus shelves pale root hairs water moss small blind flowers

Block4: The place changes even if the PCs stand still. Local people, creatures, weather, signage, and ward behavior all keep moving around the scene. Loud movement can expose homes. Treating Underroot as exotic ruins dehumanizes it. Corporate route pressure may reach even here. A lantern is covered all at once. A root door closes before the party sees who moved it. Let the place be funny through overconfident signage, awkward forms, stubborn local habits, and magic that refuses corporate language.
